# 3 Maccabees Chapter 7 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Alexandrinus) | **Section:** Liberation, Celebration, and Return

---

**7:1** When the king had written this letter to the generals in each of the cities with such instructions, he dismissed the Jews to return to their homes.

**7:2** He gave orders that the soldiers who were scattered throughout the cities should treat the Jews with respect and honor.

**7:3** He also gave orders that all the property belonging to the Jews that had been confiscated was to be restored to them intact, and that those in authority over any of their property were to return it immediately, without any subterfuge.

**7:4** Furthermore he gave orders that those who had committed any offense against them were to be punished, and that those who had spoken against them were to receive the punishment they deserved.

**7:5** And he urged his officials to deal with all the Jews in their territory with all kindness and goodwill.

**7:6** After the king had issued this letter, the Jews gathered together at a convenient place in great joy and began to celebrate with prayers and songs of praise.

**7:7** They established that day as a festival of great rejoicing, full of gladness, calling it a day of great salvation.

**7:8** The king also granted them a three-day celebration, in which they had a great feast with singing and with toasting one another.

**7:9** And the Jews who had been taken away to various places in Egypt returned home with joy and gladness.

**7:10** They had been delivered from death itself, and now they went back to their families and their houses.

**7:11** And from that day forward they resolved to celebrate that day as a day of great joy, while they dwelt in Egypt.

**7:12** They also sent letters to their brothers in Jerusalem, reporting all that had happened, and calling the day a festival.

**7:13** And they all rejoiced together for the great works that God had done for the people of Israel, showing that he is with them and looks after them.

**7:14** The Jews who had been delivered gathered together and resolved to observe that festival in their community in perpetuity, in all the places where they might live.

**7:15** They called it the Phruraia, the feast of salvation, a day of joy and gladness.

**7:16** And the glory of the God of Israel was proclaimed among all the people.

**7:17** For the God of Israel is the God who works wonders among men, and he has delivered his people from destruction.

**7:18** Blessed is the Lord who has delivered Israel from all its troubles.

**7:19** And the people of Israel praised God with thanksgiving and joyful songs of praise.

**7:20** Great is the glory of the God of Israel, who alone does wondrous things among his people.
